title: Concurrent vs Sequential
prompt: Implement async def slow_double(n) awaiting asyncio.sleep(0.1) and returning n*2. Then async def run_concurrent(values) using asyncio.create_task for each value and awaiting all tasks. Provide sync wrapper run_all(values) returning the list of results (in input order).
boilerplate:
import asyncio

async def slow_double(n):
    pass

async def run_concurrent(values):
    pass

def run_all(values):
    pass

tests.name: results match input order
tests.hint: Collect each task with await; task order = result order here.

tests.name: actually concurrent (fast, not 3x slow)
tests.code:
import time
start = time.monotonic()
run_all([1, 2, 3, 4])
elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
assert elapsed < 0.35, f'too slow: {elapsed}'
tests.hint: Four 0.1s waits overlapped must finish well under 0.4s.
